description:
Data Engineer

The Opportunity:

As a data scientist, you’re excited at the prospect of unlocking the secrets held by a data set, and you’re fascinated by the possibilities presented by IoT, machine learning, and artificial intelligence. In an increasingly connected world, massive amounts of structured and unstructured data open new opportunities. As a data scientist at Booz Allen, you can help turn these complex data sets into useful information to solve global challenges. Across private and public sectors—from fraud detection to cancer research to national intelligence—we need you to help find the answers in the data.

On our team, you’ll use your analytical skills and data science knowledge to create real-world impact. You’ll work closely with your clients to understand their questions and needs, and then dig into their data-rich environments to find the pieces of their information puzzle. You’ll develop algorithms and systems and use the right combination of tools and frameworks to turn sets of disparate data points into objective answers to help clients make informed decisions. Ultimately, you’ll provide a deep understanding of the data, what it all means, and how it can be used.

Work with us as we use data science for good.

Join us. The world can’t wait.

3+ years of experience developing and maintaining machine learning, AI‑driven, or data‑centric applications

Secret clearance
HS diploma or GED

3+ years of experience with Python, SQL, or TypeScript in data or ML engineering contexts
3+ years of experience with UI and UX design
3+ years of experience working with geospatial datasets, spatial analytics, or geospatial ML workflows
3+ years of experience with distributed data and compute ecosystems, such as Spark, Databricks, Hadoop, Hive, AWS EMR, and Kafka, for large‑scale ML workloads
Experience operating in a Combatant Command or international mission‑focused environment and applying DS or ML methods to operational decision‑making

title: AI Automation Lead (m/f/d)
description:
Location: Böblingen (Germany)


Job Purpose
The AI Automation Lead drives FutureLog's AI-first transformation outside of engineering — designing, building, and embedding automation and AI-enabled workflows across internal business processes such as Operations, HR and Finance. This is a hands-on, technical role first and a strategist second: the Lead personally builds and ships automations rather than only designing and delegating them, working close to the ground the way a forward-deployed engineer would.


This role operates horizontally across functions it does not own, partnering with Operations, HR and Finance leadership to identify, prioritize, and deliver high-value automation. Delivery is only half the job: the role also builds the internal capability and habits that let those functions keep improving on their own — a community of practice, upskilled managers, and enough grass-roots momentum that AI adoption doesn't depend solely on this one person.
The role reports directly to the CTO as a deliberate strategic lever for company-wide AI adoption.


General Tasks and Responsibilities

- Transformation agenda: Develop and maintain an ambitious internal AI transformation plan, sequenced and negotiated jointly with sponsoring function leaders.
- Process discovery & prioritization: Map automation opportunities across Operations, HR and Finance, and other internal operations; prioritize by cost/time savings, risk, and strategic value
- Hands-on delivery & tooling: Personally design, build, and ship AI-enabled workflow automations using low-code platforms (e.g. n8n, Langdock, Power Automate).
- Change management & adoption: Drive adoption of new automated workflows within the receiving teams, including training, documentation, and process redesign — delivery is not complete until the function actually works differently.
- Community & upskilling: Build communities of practice around AI-enabled ways of working; upskill managers directly so adoption compounds rather than staying dependent on this one role.
- Stakeholder partnership: Co-design changes with the functional owners of each process (Operations, HR and Finance), since the processes themselves belong to other departments, not this role.
- Governance & compliance: Ensure automations meet data-protection, security, and audit requirements (GDPR, ISO 27001), coordinating with IT & Security on access, data handling, and no-training-on-customer-data constraints.
- Measurement, reporting & self-funding: Define and track ROI/impact metrics (hours saved, cost avoided, error/exception rate) per initiative; operate the function as self-funding — efficiencies found are reinvested to grow the team, which is how it earns its next hires rather than through a standing budget ask. Report progress and roadmap directly to the CTO.


Qualifications

- Technical fluency, first and foremost: Hands-on ability to personally build and debug automations end-to-end with low-code workflow/AI platforms (e.g. n8n, Langdock, Power Automate), plus enough scripting/API skill to go beyond their limits when needed — this is a technical-expert role, not a strategy/consulting role with automation as a topic. The team starts as one person, so the Lead has to be the builder, not just the architect.
- Professional experience: Proven delivery of business-process automation or AI-enabled workflow projects in a cross-functional setting spanning Operations, HR and Finance — not purely an IT/engineering background.
- Stakeholder influence: Demonstrated ability to drive change with senior stakeholders who do not report to them, securing buy-in and adoption without formal line authority.
- Change management: Experience running adoption/change programs and building lasting capability (communities of practice, enablement/upskilling), not only shipping the automation itself.
- Business acumen: Working understanding of Operations, HR and Finance processes sufficient to identify credible high-value automation targets and evaluate operational risk.
- Data protection awareness: Understanding of GDPR and data-handling constraints relevant to applying AI to internal and company data.
- fluent in English and German


Behavioural Characteristics

- Hands-on bias: Genuinely prefers building and shipping over presenting plans; treats "technical expert" as core identity, not a secondary skill behind the strategy.
- Influence without authority: Builds trust and credibility with executives and process owners across departments they do not manage.
- Leads by example: Visibly adopts and models the AI-enabled ways of working being asked of others, starting with their own habits and FutureLog's leadership/management layer.
- Bias to action: Ships pragmatic automations quickly rather than waiting for perfect processes or full consensus.
- Multiplies through others: Builds community and upskills managers rather than keeping all delivery capacity personally bottlenecked.
